C1.rationale: Anchor Level 1: 'Collaboration/teamwork appears in learning outcomes, but no core unit assesses it.' Teamwork/collaboration recurs as a generic-skill outcome across nearly every core subject ('work collaboratively'; 'Work in collaboration with others') but no assessed core task is quoted as requiring coordinating work across people and tools/AI systems, or as a group project, client/stakeholder work, or interprofessional activity judged on its own criteria. Two Level-2 candidates were considered and resolved downward: WELF90018's 'Written peer evaluation' is appraisal of a peer's quality of work, which homes in C2 under the one-construct-one-home rule, not here; and Placement's 'liaising with other professional practitioners' is descriptive subject-overview text, not a quoted assessed criterion.
evidenceLines: work collaboratively;
Work in collaboration with others.

C2.rationale: Anchor Level 2: 'Core assessment includes criterion-referenced appraisal of quality: peer review, structured critique, portfolio with standards, marking against exemplars.' A 30%-weighted 'Written self-evaluation' is assessed in nearly every core subject, and WELF90018 additionally assesses a 'Written peer evaluation' (30%), matching the ILO 'Constructively appraise their practice and the practice of others'. Level 3 ('document and justify reliance decisions... or evidence strategy adjustment over time') is not clearly reached: the extract contains no reliance-on-tool/source/collaborator content, and the nearest candidates (WELF90018's six-weekly reflective journal; placement's supervisor-guided reflection) are not quoted as a graded, criterion-referenced justification of strategy adjustment, so this was scored to the lower level.
evidenceLines: Written self-evaluation
Constructively appraise their practice and the practice of others.
Written peer evaluation

C3.rationale: Anchor Level 0: 'No digital/AI content in any core unit or program-level outcome.' Across the course overview and all ten core/capstone subjects, the only digital-adjacent language is communication modality ('Communicate effectively in oral and digital forms') — the medium of delivery, not digital or AI tool use, capability, limitation, ethics or governance. No AI or digital-literacy content of any kind appears in the extract.
evidenceLines: Communicate effectively in oral and digital forms;

C4.rationale: DEMOTED from 3 to 2 on adversarial verification. The level-3 route relies on WELF90023's intended learning outcome ('Design a personalised professional development plan...') for the 'knowledge gaps' requirement; the actual assessment-table line ('Professional development plan/oral assessment. (25 minutes)') never itself states gap-identification as a graded criterion. R2 requires assessment evidence, not an outcome statement standing in for it.
evidenceLines: Design a personalised professional development plan that aligns with the standards and the requirements of practice placements and future professional counselling work.
Evaluate and apply supervisor, peer, and client feedback to develop clinical readiness for counselling settings including the placement experience;
Professional development plan/oral assessment. (25 minutes)
design of a client-facing tool, training module, policy submission, service enhancement plan, or business case to establish a private practice.

C5.rationale: DEMOTED from 2 to 1 on adversarial verification. The capstone overview text (not quoted in the score) states the research strategy is developed 'such as a scoping review or analysis of secondary data' -- neither involves primary data collection, closer to the level-1 anchor 'literature-review assessment'. The rationale omits this countervailing evidence sitting next to the quoted ILO and does not disclose the ambiguity.
evidenceLines: Students will have the opportunity to undertake a literature review, develop research questions and undertake the research activities required to answer their research question.
Design and implement an appropriate research method to answer the research question;
Oral defence. Due in week 7 of Part B.
25 credit point capstone experience comprised of a practice innovation or research capstone pathway.

W1.rationale: DEMOTED from 3 to 2 on adversarial verification. 'Professional conduct or accountability explicitly among the assessed criteria' is evidenced only by the Australian Police Check / Working With Children Check requirement, which is an eligibility prerequisite to attend placement, not a graded performance criterion. No quoted line shows conduct/accountability actually being marked; level 2 (real-practitioner-judged professional genre via supervisor observation) is solidly met, but level 3's second conjunct is not.
evidenceLines: Students will undertake Counselling Placement A in a professional counselling context, guided by an approved counselling supervisor.
both comprise on the job demonstration by the student and observation by the placement supervisor.
Students must complete an Australian Police Check and relevant state-based screening (e.g. Working With Children or Working With Vulnerable People Checks) to undertake placement.

W2.rationale: Anchor Level 3: authentic tasks form the assessment spine (at least one per stage) AND at least one carries a genuine constraint of practice. Authentic, practice-resembling artefacts recur across stages: WELF90018's recorded 'Counselling skills demonstration recording and oral presentation'; WELF90023's 'Simulated 15 minute counselling session'; Placement's real client work ('direct counselling delivery, case presentation, record keeping, managing a caseload... liaising with other professional practitioners', structured as 'a 2 days per week for 7 weeks of placement'); and the capstone's practitioner artefact ('design of a client-facing tool, training module, policy submission, service enhancement plan, or business case'). Placement supplies the genuine constraint of practice: real clients, a fixed weekly structure. Ambiguity: the recurring 'Case study/Scenario based oral assessment' format used across most Year 1 subjects reads as an academic oral exam about a scenario rather than the artefact a practitioner produces, so it was not counted toward the spine; the score rests on the other four instances instead.
evidenceLines: Counselling skills demonstration recording and oral presentation
Simulated 15 minute counselling session during residential experience week.
direct counselling delivery, case presentation, record keeping, managing a caseload, and liaising with other professional practitioners.
Placements will usually be structured as a 2 days per week for 7 weeks of placement.
design of a client-facing tool, training module, policy submission, service enhancement plan, or business case to establish a private practice.

W3.rationale: Anchor Level 3: substantial required work-situated learning, a sequence, in the core, supervised by a practitioner, assessed, with accountability to the host and structured reflection. 'All students must complete a compulsory, in-person 200-hour supervised placement under the guidance of a qualified clinical supervisor', delivered as a required two-subject sequence: 'Counselling Placement B provides 105 hours of professional practice, which combined with 105 hours in Counselling Placement A leads to a total of 210 placement hours', with Placement B gated on completion of Placement A. Structured reflection is explicit assessed ILO content across both subjects.
evidenceLines: All students must complete a compulsory, in-person 200-hour supervised placement under the guidance of a qualified clinical supervisor.
Counselling Placement B provides 105 hours of professional practice, which combined with 105 hours in Counselling Placement A leads to a total of 210 placement hours in the Master of Counselling.
Students must have completed the Counselling Placement A to be eligible for subject.
Show preparation for and engagement in supervision, guided self-reflection and professional development opportunities;
Students will engage in structured supervision, feedback, and critical self-reflection to further develop and consolidate their counselling skills.

G1.rationale: The program documents an all-compulsory specialist core ('125 credit points of Compulsory subjects') with a staged prerequisite chain: the Residential subject 'provides preparation for placements and needs to be completed before Placement A', and Placement B is gated ('Students must have completed the Counselling Placement A to be eligible for subject') — a coherent, progressively deepening counselling-specific sequence from theory/skills/ethics/assessment through residential, dual placement, and capstone.
evidenceLines: 125 credit points of Compulsory subjects
The Residential Industry Experience subject provides preparation for placements and needs to be completed before Placement A.
Students must have completed the Counselling Placement A to be eligible for subject.

G2.rationale: Core assessment repeatedly requires defended, scenario-based decisions under pass/fail hurdles ('Case study/Scenario based oral assessment' with 'Hurdle requirement: Students must achieve a Pass for this hurdle'), and the required placement sequence places students in live, uncertain practice with real clients and real-time simulation ('Practical experience... extending their development of counselling skills with real-world experience and the varied clients they will work within professional practice'; 'Simulated 15 minute counselling session during residential experience week').
evidenceLines: Case study/Scenario based oral assessment.
Hurdle requirement: Students must achieve a Pass for this hurdle.

Practical experience is important for a student's counselling education, extending their development of counselling skills with real-world experience and the varied clients they will work within professional practice.
Simulated 15 minute counselling session during residential experience week.

ambiguities: C1: WELF90018's 'Written peer evaluation' (30%) and Placement's descriptive 'liaising with other professional practitioners' could suggest Level 2 collaborative/interprofessional practice; resolved to Level 1 — peer evaluation is homed in C2 (appraisal of quality) per the one-construct-one-home rule, and the placement liaison language is not a quoted assessed criterion.

C2: WELF90018's six-weekly reflective journal and placement's supervisor-guided reflection gesture toward Level 3's 'evidence strategy adjustment over time', but neither is quoted as a graded, criterion-referenced justification of reliance/strategy decisions; resolved to Level 2.

C4: The Practice Innovation capstone's suggested project list ('client-facing tool, training module, policy submission, service enhancement plan, business case') is somewhat bounded rather than fully open-scoped; the Level 3 score rests primarily on the independently unambiguous WELF90023 professional-development-plan evidence. Verification demoted this item to Level 2 — see rationale.

C5: The Research Capstone pathway shows Level-3-caliber content (methodology defended via a hurdle-linked oral defence), but the capstone is 'comprised of a practice innovation or research capstone pathway' — an OR choice — and the Level 3 anchor explicitly excludes 'one route among several'; resolved to Level 2. Verification demoted this item to Level 1 — see rationale.

W1/W3: Both draw on the Counselling Placement A/B sequence. W1 is scored from the audience/practitioner-judgement and professional-conduct clauses (supervisor observation, police-check compliance); W3 is scored from the duration/structure/accountability clauses (210 required hours, prerequisite sequencing, structured reflection) — distinct constructs per instrument design, not double-counted from the same evidence.

W1/W2: Both draw on placement text. W1 uses the audience/practitioner-judgement clauses; W2 uses the task-content and constraint-of-practice clauses (real clients, fixed weekly structure) — kept to separate homes. Verification demoted W1 to Level 2 — see rationale.
Verification pass 2026-08-30: C4, C5 and W1 were demoted from the submitted scores on adversarial review; see each item's rationale for the specific reasoning.
